chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Muhammad Bin Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The divorced woman waits in her house and it is not befitting for her that she goes out until she has fulfilled her waiting period; and her waiting period is of three Quroos (pure periods), or three months, except if she happens to menstruate.
ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period (Iddah) for a divorced woman according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) in al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'iqamah al-bayt' (residence in the home) as a primary condition for the Iddah of a divorced woman, emphasizing seclusion to preserve lineage and dignity. While the text specifies three menstrual cycles or three months, Shia jurisprudence further distinguishes between pre-menopausal women and those who do not menstruate, reflecting the nuanced application of this ruling in fiqh.
